title: A section was closed, but the feeder was overloaded: what changed after removing the common compensation
description: Conditional example of withdrawing a section: active power decreased, but removing the common reactive power compensation increased the apparent power of the retained production.
seo_title: Closing a section and reactive power compensation: why the load increased
seo_description: Before withdrawing the section, apparent power was 120.93 kVA; after — 125 kVA with a limit of 123. We analyse the error of judging only by the reduction in kilowatts.
seo_keywords: withdrawing a section common reactive power compensation
increase in apparent power after dismantling
work boundaries when closing a section
content:
After closing one section, the load on the common feeder may increase even if active power consumption decreased. This will happen in our conditional example if, together with the section, the reactive power compensation located there, which also served the retained production, is removed. The error here is not in the name of the room: the common function has a specific numerical result that is lost on withdrawal.

Two confirmed configurations instead of assumptions

The enterprise closes section A; the neighbouring section B must continue operating in the previous mode. On the common side of the feeder, an agreed limit of 123 kVA applies to the mode under consideration. This is a condition of the specific example, not a standard power rating for operating enterprises.

Before the changes, section A consumes 20 kW of active power with no reactive component. Section B consumes 100 kW and 75 kvar of inductive reactive power. The compensating device K-1 provides the opposite component of 60 kvar. Although K-1 is physically located in room A, the relevant diagram confirms its operation on the common feeder, not only on the local load A.

In the proposed withdrawal variant, both load A and K-1 are removed. Mode B remains unchanged: 100 kW and 75 kvar. The attribution of the numbers to one point and one considered mode is established. For the educational model, sinusoidal voltage and current are given, and losses not included in the named powers are not added separately. This allows comparing the two states without substituting the initial conditions.

Calculation before and after withdrawal

Before the change, the total active power P equals 20 + 100 = 120 kW. The reactive component Q on the common side equals 75 − 60 = 15 kvar. The apparent power S in the adopted model is defined as √(P² + Q²): √(120² + 15²) = √14625, i.e. approximately 120.93 kVA.

This result is less than the set 123 kVA. The margin against the considered limit is about 2.07 kVA. It refers specifically to the initial mode including the operation of K-1. The device cannot be crossed out of the diagram while leaving its effect in the numbers.

After removing A and K-1, the active power became 100 kW. But the reactive component is now not 15 but 75 kvar. We get S = √(100² + 75²) = √15625 = 125 kVA. This is 2 kVA above the limit set for the example.

The conclusion is definite: the proposed state does not confirm compliance with the common feeder limit. A reduction in active power by 20 kW does not mean a reduction in all significant load characteristics. In our calculation, apparent power increased by about 4.07 kVA.

The change is also visible in the P/S ratio: before withdrawal it is about 0.992, after — 0.8. Therefore the previous power factor cannot be left in the final calculation and multiplied only by the new kilowatts. This would preserve the effect of the already removed compensation in the model.

Where the error arose in the dismantling statement

The author of the statement attributed K-1 entirely to the closing section by its installation location. Only the phrase "after withdrawing A the load decreases from 120 to 100 kW" remained in the explanation. The phrase about active power itself is correct, but an unjustified conclusion was drawn from it about compliance with the limit specified in kVA.

The Electrical Installation Guide by Schneider Electric gives the relationship between active, reactive and apparent power for sinusoidal conditions. The comparison was performed using this relationship. In a non-sinusoidal mode, the same two-component formula cannot be mechanically declared a sufficient description of all components: the conditions of our example are stated in advance.

It is also incorrect to arithmetically subtract 60 kvar from 120 kW or to add them into one number without defining the quantity. In the initial state, 60 kvar are already accounted for with the compensation sign in Q. After removing K-1, this component must be excluded from the balance, not retained merely because it was present in the previous table.

What result to pass to the decision developer

"The proposed withdrawal of A includes removal of K-1, which participates in the common compensation. At the given unchanged mode B, the calculated apparent power on the considered side of the feeder rises from 120.93 to 125 kVA. The limit of 123 kVA is not met by the new state. Justification only by the reduction of active power to 100 kW is insufficient."

From this record it follows that the proposed final state and its justification should be reviewed. It does not automatically prescribe keeping K-1 switched on, moving it or installing another battery. The suitability of the compensation, the modes, the protection and the necessary technical changes are considered in the relevant decision, not determined by a single school formula.

Therefore, the work boundary cannot be accepted based only on the plan of the closing room. In this case, a specific retained function is already known and the consequence of its loss is shown. To discuss a similar interface, send to NPI "Nedra" the diagram of the common function and the calculation of two proposed states.
